newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga sees Vigdis oil restart early Aug.
newsitem.headline: Saga sees Vigdis oil restart early Aug.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday it hoped to restart oil production at the North Sea Vigdis development in early August.
Vigdis was shut in on July 17 due to a fault in the gas compressor system.
The field, which came on stream in January five months ahead of schedule, has suffered a series of shutdowns since April due a fault in the compressor system.
"According to the plan we have today, the start up of oil production at Vigdis will be at the beginning of August," Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag told Reuters.
"The gas compressor system will be started two days after oil production has resumed."
The field had been producing around 40,000 barrels per day before the latest incident. Since the development came on stream it has pumped around three million barrels of oil.
Schibevaag emphasised there was nothing at fault with the oil production system. Due to Norwegian regulations on gas flaring, crude production at Vigdis is dependent on the gas compressor system.
